title: MediatR
description: A simple mediator implementation for in-process messaging, enabling CQRS and mediator patterns.

data.text: MediatR is a simple implementation of the mediator pattern for in-process messaging. It enables you to send requests, publish notifications, and stream responses without direct references between senders and handlers.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install MediatR and the dependency injection extension.
data.code:
dotnet add package MediatR
dotnet add package MediatR.Extensions.Microsoft.DependencyInjection

data.content: Define a request handler and publish a notification.

terms.definition: A behavioral pattern that centralizes communication between components.
Command Query Responsibility Segregation - separating read and write operations.

data.title: Best Practice
data.text: Use MediatR to decouple controllers from business logic in ASP.NET Core applications.

MediatR decouples a controller from the handler that does the work. A request implements `IRequest<TResponse>` and is handled by an `IRequestHandler<TRequest, TResponse>` resolved from DI. A notification implements `INotification` and can have many handlers, each invoked when it is published.

data.title: A command handler and a notification
Interview angle: pipeline behaviors are middleware for handlers
data.text: An `IPipelineBehavior` wraps every handler, which is where cross-cutting concerns belong: validation, logging, transactions, and caching. That is why MediatR shows up in clean-architecture samples — it centralizes the concerns that would otherwise be repeated in each handler. Be ready to say what it costs, too: an extra layer of indirection and a dispatch that is less obvious than a direct method call.

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: MediatR is essential for implementing CQRS and the mediator pattern in .NET.
